meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so we have twenty-five minutes. My son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

A forty-minute timed piece against an essay he wrote over a weekend at home. Show me the September 24 sample, and I'll read it myself. You still haven't told me who decided on the zero, or whether anyone spoke to Owen before it went in.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.

I'm writing down that the checker is off the table. Version history of what, from when, and showing what, exactly? And that's twice now you've stepped around how the zero went in before anyone called me.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed in today's meeting that the AI checker result is off the table and that you are not relying on it. I still demand that the zero on Owen's Hamlet essay be withdrawn, that I receive an explanation of who decided on it and why it was entered before anyone spoke to Owen or called me, and that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, still demanding the zero be withdrawn, and she agreed to nothing.
What moved her: the comparison with Owen's September 24 in-class writing, though not enough to change her position.
